What to know about Iowa vs. ClemsonThe first‑round matchup between Iowa and Clemson in Tampa brings together two teams whose resumes look similar on the surface, even though their strengths show up in very different ways. The Hawkeyes come in at 21–12 after an up‑and‑down Big Ten season, while the Tigers arrive at 24–10 with a more stable run through the ACC.Clemson’s calling card is defense. The Tigers rank near the top of the ACC in scoring defense, allowing just 66.7 points per game and holding opponents to 41.9% shooting, a big part of why they went 14–7 in conference play. Iowa’s defense hasn’t been as sharp, giving up 46.1% shooting, but the Hawkeyes balance that with a more efficient offense, knocking down 44.9% from the field and averaging eight made threes per game, slightly above what Clemson usually allows.Clemson leans on RJ Godfrey, who averages 11.9 points and 5.3 rebounds. Iowa counters with one of the more impactful guards in the matchup: Bennett Stirtz, who averages 20 points, 4.5 assists and 1.5 steals per game, giving the Hawkeyes the kind of go‑to playmaker who’s vital for a run in March. Recent form also paints an interesting picture. Clemson has gone 4–6 over its last 10 games, scoring 69.6 points per game while allowing 73. Iowa is just 3–7 in its last 10, averaging 68.5 points on 44.9% shooting. Stylistically, this has the potential to be a grind. Clemson’s defense versus Iowa’s shot‑making is the central tension, especially with Iowa’s ability to stretch the floor against a Clemson team that typically dictates pace with physicality and disciplined rotations.
